observation.visible_scene: A dark shadow of an open hand (palm, four extended fingers and a thumb) is cast on a light-toned wooden surface. A warm, bright light source comes from the right, producing a glowing patch and a diagonal shadow edge at the upper left. The hand shadow occupies the center-left of the frame throughout.
visible_changes: The thumb portion of the shadow changes shape over the excerpt: it begins as a long, clearly separated protrusion pointing down-right (frames 1–11), then retracts and shortens toward the palm edge around t≈0.88–1.04 s (frames 12–13), stays drawn-in/short through roughly t≈2.4 s (frames 13–31), and extends outward again into a longer protrusion from about t≈2.48 s to the end (frames 32–41).
The palm and the four finger lobes of the shadow remain essentially in the same position and shape the whole time; only the thumb lobe visibly deforms.

The wooden background, the bright light patch on the right, and the upper-left shadow edge do not move, indicating a static camera and static surface; the observed change is deformation of the shadow (thumb), not translation of the whole shadow or camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual hand producing the shadow is not visible, only its silhouette; the unseen operator's motion and intent are not shown.
Whether the thumb was already mid-retraction before t=0 or continues to move after t=3.2 s is outside the cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Minor apparent jitter in the finger-tip outlines between adjacent frames may be compression/lighting noise rather than real motion.
The exact timing of the thumb's re-extension (between frames 31 and 32) is approximate given the 0.08 s sampling.
